brief.headline: Close the ₹1.26 Cr gap: benchmark Gujarat Ambuja's Dextrose to Sayaji's ₹66.48/KG and lock volume in exchange for price.

priceAsk.basis: We already pay Sayaji Industries Limited ₹66.48/KG for identical Dextrose; Gujarat Ambuja runs 3.0% higher, costing us ₹1.26 Cr annually in excess. The India export unit value sits at 42.95 ₹/kg, so there is substantial room below our ask.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Hold at 30 Days After Receipt; no extension

brief.financialLeverage: Gujarat Ambuja is financially robust—revenue of ₹6031.59 Cr, net margin of 6.9%, EBITDA margin of 10.1%, and very low leverage at 0.13x debt-to-equity. Our ₹21.21 Cr spend is just 0.35% of their revenue, so we are not a make-or-break account. However, their 23.5%/yr revenue growth signals they prize volume gains, and their B health score (70/100) with no risk flags means they can absorb a price concession to defend share. Push firmly on price; they have the margin and the motive.

evidence.point: We pay Gujarat Ambuja ₹68.45/KG for Dextrose, yet Sayaji Industries delivers the same material at a lower rate
The price gap costs us annually in avoidable excess spend
For Dextrose Anhydrous IP specifically, the gap versus best price is identical
Gujarat Ambuja's EBITDA margin shows they earn well above basic commodity economics
They are growing fast, which means new volume is strategically valuable to them
The global reference price for Dextrose exports from India is far below even our target ask

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist (starch, dextrose) with growing capacity and B health score—credible drop-in source to balance the 56% share Gujarat Ambuja holds.

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker; established dextrose/sorbitol supplier and a proven alternate to Gujarat Ambuja.

alternates.name: Roquette India Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Indian arm of global starch major Roquette with pharma-grade dextrose capability—premium quality and very reliable if Gujarat Ambuja will not move.

risks: We source 56% of our Dextrose—₹21.21 Cr—through Gujarat Ambuja, creating single-source concentration; walking away without a qualified alternate is operationally risky.
At 0.35% of their ₹6031.59 Cr revenue, we lack account-level leverage; they can afford to lose us if we overplay our hand.
Their strong financials (10.1% EBITDA, 0.13x leverage, no risk flags) mean they do not face margin or liquidity pressure that would force a quick concession.
Payment terms are already at 30 Days After Receipt and not flagged as worst-in-class, so there is no working-capital lever to pull in parallel.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership and the volume we place with you, but we're carrying a ₹1.26 Cr cost disadvantage on Dextrose versus Sayaji at ₹66.48/KG—let's close that gap and talk about locking in higher committed volume going forward.
